summary: The note describes a growing trend of student-led historical archiving projects, from a Somerset high school time capsule to a university digital repository, along with workshops, technology seminars, community outreach, cross-school collaboration and ethics efforts. These projects teach research skills while preserving local and institutional history. The note closes with proposals for dedicated archival curriculums and calls this a possible golden age of student-led archiving.
one_line: Students worldwide are leading archival initiatives, from time capsules and digital repositories to consortia and ethics councils, between September 2023 and March 2024.
key_facts: On September 2, 2023, Martin High School in Somerset unveiled the Somerset Time Capsule Initiative, a project of its historical society.
The Somerset Time Capsule Initiative was led by students under history teacher Mrs. Lydia Cartwright and compiled artifacts, photographs and personal narratives into a digital time capsule.
From October 5, 2023, the Martin High School Historical Society and the Somerset Community Council launched a series of archiving workshops.

Historical consultant and archivist Mr. Philip Stephens gave practical instruction to faculty and students from various schools in the workshops, covering classification, preservation methods and digitization.

The Alexandria Project was inaugurated on November 15, 2023, by university students Emily Chen and Jonathan Rivera of the University of Historica, and is named after the ancient Library of Alexandria.

The Alexandria Project aims to build a comprehensive digital repository of manuscripts, letters and newspapers from the university's founding to the present, with a collaborative platform for students across departments.

On December 1, 2023, the seminar "The Digital Archivist's Toolkit" at the Annual Conference on Historical Preservation showcased metadata tagging, OCR for handwritten notes and climate-controlled environments.
Westbridge High School, led by student historian Marie Watson, launched the "Heritage Voices" campaign on January 20, 2024, inviting residents to share stories, documents and photographs.

On February 10, 2024, representatives from ten schools formed the Interscholastic Historical Consortium to create a unified archival system for sharing yearbooks, academic journals and institutional records.

The Conversation of Histories Ethical Council (CHEC) was established on March 3, 2024, by Historica Community College students to promote consent, privacy and respectful treatment of cultural resources.
Student efforts have sparked discussion of dedicated curriculums for historical documentation and archiving to ensure a steady stream of young archivists.
